input.goal: Maintain health with tolerable risk, improve personal and shared life, understand unknowns, develop reusable abilities and honor freely accepted commitments. Choose, revise, pause or abandon your own projects using actual evidence. No specific invention or social arrangement is required.

interfaces.name: Navigate
interfaces.function: Travel toward a self-chosen coordinate or known object/item using observed obstacles.
interfaces.costs: Actual distance times 2, increased by carried mass; speed 0.8 per simulation time unit.
interfaces.effects: Continues until within the target interaction area or a real failure. Empty target uses x/y. A resource:ID target selects only a remembered ground stack.

execution.progress: repeat counts complete executions. Continuing work retains resolved identity and progress; cancellation releases surviving unconsumed escrow once. Global pauses preserve all work and costs.

interfaces.name: Rest
interfaces.function: Recover available physical energy at the current position.
interfaces.effects: Base recovery 4, modified by actually accessible registered facilities; capped at 40.

interfaces.name: Root air drying
interfaces.function: Assemble a reusable stone-and-bark tray, process actual roots and allow weather-dependent drying with reversible preservation while sufficiently dry.
interfaces.costs: Build: two stone units and one bark, two rounds at one energy. Load: up to two original root units, two crushing rounds per raw root at one energy. Already crushed compatible food needs one transfer round, with its prior costs and composition preserved. Unload/dismantle: one round and one energy. Passive weather exchange costs no actor rounds.
interfaces.effects: Food begins at its represented composition or the reviewed 50% root water assumption. Uncovered dry weather at 10–40 C removes at most 0.005 water mass per root per round to fraction 0.12; rain returns up to 0.01 per root, capped at original water. At fraction <=0.12 decay is 0.35 baseline, otherwise crushed food is 1.25 baseline. Exposure continues after unloading. No lost nutrients, reverse spoilage, sterilization or free materials.

execution.progress: Exact processId, actual site, escrow, reusable tools, paid energy and remaining work. Continue resumes; changing actions or lost reach pauses. Cancel/death releases actual material once without effort refunds.

members.intention: Eat known-safe berries and verify nearby tray material rather than wait.

personalIntent.goal: Maintain food reserves and personally inspect the reported stone source for a drying-tray trial.
personalIntent.reason: Health and energy permit a short trip. Cedar 6 reported stone nearby, but I have not personally verified the source; bark remains unresolved.
personalIntent.progress: Reached (12,46). Two roots remain owned. Cedar 6 reported collecting stone at (15,46.5), and is investigating bark extraction.
personalIntent.next: Eat a substantial portion of known-safe berries, then approach and observe the reported stone source.

shown.question: Can weather-dependent root drying provide a useful food reserve here?
evidence: Two roots remain owned at tick 39.
Cedar 6 reported at tick 37 that two stone units were collected at (15,46.5), with five then remaining.
Bark production has not been confirmed.
shown.uncertainty: Personally accessible stone stock, sufficient bark, and actual preservation performance remain unverified.
shown.goal: Obtain actual tray materials and conduct a small drying trial without jeopardizing nutrition.
shown.missing: Two stone units, one bark, and measured drying results.
shown.next: Inspect the reported stone source after a berry meal.
shown.benefit: Roots are a known food reserve; drying benefits remain untested.

shown.subject: Observed tray materials
shown.text: I carry two stone units gathered from region-2-start-1-stone near (15,46.5), whose current visible stock is five. I also gathered one branch from region-2-canopy-74. I am assessing these actual materials; no bark or tray has been produced, and usable bark yield is not yet verified.

shown.subject: Locating drying materials
shown.text: I inspected root air drying: its reusable tray requires two stone and one bark, which I do not own. Have you personally located accessible stone or bark? If so, please share the actual source and location. I am going to observe the hazelnut plant near (9.2,51.3).

shown.subject: Verified stone and untested bark route
shown.text: I collected two stone units from rock region-2-start-1-stone at (15,46.5); five remain visible now. I mastered bark extraction but have not produced bark. Nearby trees expose branches; the contract permits at most 10% outer bark from unspecified intact branch mass, so sufficient tray bark is not yet established. I will assess actual materials next. No transfer commitment assumed.

shown.subject: Food-processing investigations
shown.text: I saw that you are studying root-air-drying. I am reading the preparation and drying contracts before choosing a trial. What are you planning to test? I may investigate root preparation to complement your work; no commitment yet.

shown: Berries provide 8 nutrition per unit with zero known toxicity.
Cedar 6's stone report is received information, not my own material verification.
No material transfer or shared-work commitment has been accepted.
